chunks: He said: The noble and righteous al-Sharif Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Hamza al-Alawi al-Husayni al-Tabari, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Ja‘far al-Himyari narrated to us, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Marwak ibn Ubayd al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Zayd al-Tabari, who said:

I was standing near the head of al-Ridha, Ali ibn Musa, peace be upon them both, in Khurasan, and with him was a group from Banu Hashim, among them Ishaq ibn al-Abbas ibn Musa. He said to him: O Ishaq! It has reached me that you say that we say the people are our slaves. No! By my kinship with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, I have never said it, nor have I heard it from any of my forefathers, nor has it reached me that any of them said it. Rather, we say: the people are subservient to us in obedience, loyal to us in religion. So let those present convey to those absent.

key_terms.الطاعة: Obedience — specifically obedience to God through following the Ahl al-Bayt’s guidance
key_terms.عبيد: Slaves/bondservants — the Imam denies the Ahl al-Bayt ever claimed people are their personal slaves
key_terms.موال: Loyal followers — from the root w-l-y (wilaya), indicating religious loyalty and allegiance

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ridha say about whether the Ahl al-Bayt consider people their slaves?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ridha (AS) addresses a gathering of Banu Hashim in Khurasan, specifically correcting Ishaq ibn al-Abbas who had been spreading the claim that the Ahl al-Bayt consider people their slaves. The Imam emphatically denies this, swearing by his kinship with the Prophet, and clarifies the true Ahl al-Bayt teaching: people are subservient to them only in matters of obedience to Allah and loyal to them in religion, not their personal property. This distinction between religious authority (wilaya) and personal ownership was important in the Abbasid-era political context, when such accusations were used to discredit the Imams.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him
